definitions.explanation: Placing oneself at the center of all things — thinking or acting as if one's own feelings, preferences, and convenience matter more than anyone else's. Almost always negative in tone. Very commonly used in the adjectival form {自己|じこ}{中心|ちゅうしん}{的|てき} ('self-centered, egocentric') to describe a person or behavior.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{自己|じこ}{中心|ちゅうしん}{的|てき}だ。
{自己|じこ}{中心|ちゅうしん}{的|てき}な{考|かんが}え{方|かた}を{改|あらた}めたほうがいい。
examples.english: You should change your self-centered way of thinking.

examples.japanese: {自己|じこ}{中心|ちゅうしん}の{人|ひと}は{周|まわ}りの{人|ひと}の{気持|きも}ちに{気|き}づかないことが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Self-centered people often fail to notice how those around them feel.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもは{発達|はったつ}の{段階|だんかい}によっては{自己|じこ}{中心|ちゅうしん}{的|てき}な{行動|こうどう}をとるのが{普通|ふつう}だと{言|い}われている。
examples.english: It is said that, depending on their stage of development, children normally behave in self-centered ways.

notes:
Composed of {自己|じこ} (self) + {中心|ちゅうしん} (center). Literally 'the self at the center.' As a standalone noun it describes the mindset; with the な-adjective suffix {的|てき} it becomes {自己|じこ}{中心|ちゅうしん}{的|てき}, the form most speakers actually use.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {自己|じこ}{中心|ちゅうしん}{的|てき}な{人|ひと}: a self-centered person
- {自己|じこ}{中心|ちゅうしん}{的|てき}な{考|かんが}え{方|かた}: a self-centered way of thinking
- {自己|じこ}{中心|ちゅうしん}{的|てき}な{行動|こうどう}: self-centered behavior
- {自己|じこ}{中心|ちゅうしん}{主義|しゅぎ}: egoism (as an ideology or principle)
- {自己|じこ}{中心|ちゅうしん}に{考|かんが}える: to think only of oneself

REGISTER AND NUANCE:
Definitely negative in social commentary and personal criticism — calling someone {自己|じこ}{中心|ちゅうしん}{的|てき} is a serious complaint. In psychology and child-development writing, however, the word is used more neutrally, as a technical term for the developmental stage in which a young child cannot yet take another person's point of view.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {自分|じぶん}{勝手|がって}: selfish, doing as one pleases — more casual and conversational, focuses on acting without consideration.
- {わがまま}: selfish, willful — an everyday word especially for children or partners; emphasizes indulging one's own wishes.
- {利己|りこ}{的|てき}: self-interested — emphasizes looking out for one's own benefit, often in a calculating way.
- {エゴイスト}: egoist — a loanword used similarly to {自己|じこ}{中心|ちゅうしん}{的|てき}{な{人|ひと}}, but more fashionable in tone.

ANTONYMS:
- {利他|りた}{的|てき}: altruistic
- {思|おも}いやりのある: considerate, thoughtful of others
